newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta's Jan-Oct government deficit up to $242.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Malta's Jan-Oct government deficit up to $242.7 mln.

text.p: Malta had a government financial deficit of Lm 86.7 million ($242.7 million) in the first 10 months of the year, up from Lm 51.3 million in the same period last year.
The Central Office of Statistics said on Tuesday that total revenue reached Lm 388.4 million by the end of October, up 2.5 percent on the same period last year.

Revenue from income tax and value added tax amounted to Lm 137.8 million compared with Lm 119.8 million last year, while social security contributions surged ahead by 5.6 percent to reach Lm 93.2 million by the end of October.
Revenue from customs and excise declined by Lm5.7 million to Lm 19.6 million.

Total expenditure during the first 10 months of the year went up by 10.5 percent on the comparable year-ago period and stood at Lm 475.1 million. The increase was devoted to recurrent expenditure, which rose by Lm 45.1 million or 12.2 percent.
During the first 10 months of the year, the government spent Lm 22.6 million in public debt servicing compared to Lm 18.0 million last year.
Although in absolute terms capital expenditure fell marginally, it represented 12.6 percent of total government expenditure against 14.2 percent during 1995, the office added.
